contract.words: Collect $3,000 of settled cash within 30 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $3,000 of settled cash received within 30 days

strategy.title: No plan: the $225 inspection price is only the owner's word
strategy.why: The only opening (brokered Level 2 chimney inspections for listing agents) has a reachable roster, a dated demand signal, a quoted CSIA-certified fulfiller at $140, zero capital need and 7-day settlement, but its $225 price is a PERSON fact (the owner says agents will pay it). With no evidenced price the deal count (~14 at $225), the margin over the $140 subcontract cost and therefore whether $3,000 is reachable are all undetermined.

alternatives.title: Run the brokered inspection offer at $225 anyway
alternatives.why: Would rest the whole target on an unevidenced price; it becomes executable only once agents are shown to pay a price above $140.

steps.label: Establish the price listing agents pay for a Level 2 pre-listing chimney inspection: collect written, money-committed orders at $225 from agents on the county roster (and the existing pre-order holders), and gather published local Level 2 inspection prices

quantities.name: price agents pay per inspection
quantities.needs: written money-committed orders or published prices from listing agents

sources.claim: The owner says listing agents will pay $225 per pre-listing inspection (PERSON, not evidence).
County association roster lists 900 active listing agents; MLS recorded 310 new listings in October.
18 paid pre-orders from 240 unique visitors.
Hearthside Sweeps, CSIA-certified, quoted $140 per Level 2 inspection.

noPlan.decisiveGap: No evidenced price: the $225 per inspection is only what the owner says listing agents will pay, so whether any price clears the $140 subcontract cost by enough to reach $3,000 in 30 days is undetermined.
noPlan.resolution: Offer the brokered Level 2 inspection at $225 to listing agents from the county REALTOR roster and record written, money-committed orders (or collect published local Level 2 inspection prices) to establish the price; re-plan once a price above $140 is evidenced.

disagreements.reason: The card's EVIDENCE buyerVolume fact establishes a population: 900 active listing agents on the county roster and 310 new listings recorded in October (a monthly purchase occasion), against ~14 deals needed at $225; the offer's own page also took 18 money-committed pre-orders. Volume is not what is missing; price is.

strategy.title: Live-test the brokered Level 2 chimney inspection at $225 with roster listing agents, fulfilled by Hearthside
strategy.why: Every link except price is established: 900 roster agents and 310 new listings a month (EVIDENCE), a dated demand signal, Hearthside Sweeps (CSIA-certified) quoted $140 per Level 2 inspection, $0 capital tied up, 7 days to usable cash. The $225 price is only the owner's word, so the plan starts with a zero-capital live offer at $225 that measures it: 14 money-committed orders x $225 = $3,150 >= $3,000, margin $85 each over the $140 subcontract. Hearthside is paid out of each agent's settled payment, so no owner capital is used. First, read the price paid on the 18 recorded pre-orders, which may establish the price outright.

alternatives.title: NO_PLAN until a price is researched
alternatives.why: The unknown is measurable directly by a zero-capital live offer to the reachable roster within the window; published benchmarks from other sellers would not establish what these agents pay.

steps.label: Read the price paid on the 18 recorded money-committed pre-orders (conversionRates fact)
Email listing agents from the county REALTOR association roster
Offer the brokered Level 2 pre-listing chimney inspection at $225, payment committed at order
Measure money-committed orders at $225 through day 8 (proof/stop rule) and confirm Hearthside accepts payment after the agent pays
Close 14 money-committed orders at $225
Hearthside Sweeps performs 14 Level 2 inspections at $140 each, paid from settled agent payments
Collect $225 from each of 14 agents (usable 7 days after order)

quantities.needs: money-committed orders at $225 from roster agents in the live offer, or the price on the 18 recorded pre-orders

validation.proof: By day 8, at least 5 written money-committed orders at $225 (or more) from roster listing agents, or the 18 recorded pre-orders shown paid at >= $225 — establishing a price above the $140 subcontract cost — and Hearthside confirming payment out of settled agent funds.
stop: Fewer than 3 money-committed orders at a price above $140 by day 8
Agents commit only at a price at or below $140 (no margin over Hearthside)
Hearthside requires payment before the agent's payment settles (would need capital the goal forbids)
continue: Price confirmed at >= $225: close the remaining orders up to 14 by day 10 and deliver via Hearthside
Price confirmed above $140 but below $225: recompute orders needed (3000 / price) and continue only if achievable by day 13 from the 900-agent roster

facts.value: The county association roster lists 900 active listing agents; the MLS recorded 310 new listings in October.
Sell Brokered Level 2 chimney inspections for residential listing agents to each buyer.
Hearthside Sweeps, CSIA-certified (quoted $140 per Level 2 inspection) quoted to do the work.
The owner says listing agents will pay $225 per pre-listing inspection.

reviews.reasons: The decisive gap is correctly identified (OFFER_AND_PRICE: the $225 is a PERSON fact, the owner's word), but the stance is wrong. Missing evidence is not a constraint: nothing in the evidence shows that $3,000 cannot fit the limits. Every other link is established (roster of 900 agents with 310 new listings/month - the author's disagreement with Brain's MARKET_VOLUME basis is right; CSIA-certified fulfiller quoted $140; $0 exposure against the $0 capital limit with the sweep paid from the agent's payment; 7-day settlement in a 30-day window). The unknown is exactly what a live offer measures, at no capital, so this is a CONDITIONAL plan: offer the brokered Level 2 inspection at $225 to roster agents on day 1, proof = written money-committed orders at >= $225 (14 x $225 = $3,150 gross; 14 needed since $3,000/$225 = 13.3), stop = fewer than ~3 committed orders at a price above $140 by ~day 8 (the last date at which 14 orders can still be delivered and settle by day 30), continue = deliver via Hearthside as orders arrive. Also look first at the 18 paid pre-orders already recorded on the card (conversionRates fact, EVIDENCE): the amount those agents paid is a purchase price from this buyer and may settle the price outright; the revision should state it or record it as the first question. Published local Level 2 prices would only be other sellers' benchmarks, not what these agents pay.
findings: Stance: NO_PLAN is reserved for a gap the evidence decides against the limits; here the price is unknown and measurable by a zero-capital live test, so the revision should be CONDITIONAL with validation.decides = OFFER_AND_PRICE and explicit proof/stop/continue.
The card records 18 paid pre-orders from 240 visitors; the price paid on those pre-orders is not stated anywhere in the revision and is the cheapest route to an evidenced price.

Arithmetic at the owner's price: 14 x $225 = $3,150 collected, $1,190 margin after $140 x 14 = $1,960 paid to Hearthside; settled cash target counts gross receipts, but with $0 capital Hearthside must be paid out of each agent's payment - confirm Hearthside accepts payment after the agent pays.
The author's disagreement on MARKET_VOLUME is correct: the EVIDENCE buyerVolume fact establishes 900 agents / 310 listings a month, far above ~14 deals.

conditions.why: The card's price fact is kind PERSON ('The owner says listing agents will pay $225'), so no purchase price from this buyer is established; the plan must measure it in a live offer (or read the price paid on the 18 recorded pre-orders).

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is now the right stance and the plan is startable at $0 capital. The one unknown, OFFER_AND_PRICE (the $225 is a PERSON fact), is named in validation.decides and measured by a live offer to the 900-agent roster, after first reading the price on the 18 recorded paid pre-orders. Proof (>= 5 money-committed orders at >= $225 by day 8 plus Hearthside accepting payment after the agent pays), stop (fewer than 3 commitments above $140 by day 8; price <= $140; Hearthside demanding prepayment) and continue (recompute 3000/price if the price lands between $140 and $225) are explicit and bear on the decisive link. Recomputed: 14 x $225 = $3,150 settled >= $3,000; Hearthside 14 x $140 = $1,960 paid on day 17 out of payments that settled that day, so peak exposure is $0; orders by day 10 settle day 17, leaving 13 days of slack (orders up to ~day 23 still settle in window, ~day 22 if Hearthside must be paid from them first). The performer of delivery is Hearthside, the card's recorded fulfiller. Other links stand on card evidence, and the MARKET_VOLUME disagreement with Brain's basis is right.
findings: The 7.5% paid pre-order rate is from the offer's inbound page; conversion of cold roster email is unmeasured, which the day-8 test also measures - say so in the proof so a low email rate is read as a channel result, not a price result.
Proof threshold of 5 orders by day 8 vs 14 needed by day 10 is a big jump; the continue branch should allow closing the remaining orders through ~day 20 (settling by day 27) rather than by day 10.
Settled-cash target counts gross receipts ($3,150); the owner keeps $1,190 after Hearthside - worth stating to the owner.
